en: Salut, Returner. I am Casmir, I've heard of you. I'm with luck: you must be good enough for what I need.
Returner.
No sudden movements.
Yes?
Hmm...
Need to talk to you.
Can we chat?
We should talk.
Want to trade.
Let's trade.
What do you have for trading?
Hm, I don't usually trade much.
Don't have much to trade for.
Got any interesting scraps?
I'll see what you have.
Don't die.
Until we meet again.
Au revoir.
Salut, Returner.
Yes yes, 'til later.
Need my services?
Need something done?
Got work for me?
Found your Work Order.
Found this on a corpse... (Give Work Order.)
Here – found this. (Give Work Order.)
You're a Mechanist. What are you doing with the Rada?

Hmph! Dubravka is the name of a pit I seem to have walked into. Working with them seemed a fine choice a couple years ago; I thought I could devote myself to making weapons for them, aligning my skills with that recent passion.
But in little time I was assigned "more urgent tasks" – fixing filters, unclogging pipes, devising systems of irrigation, sanitation, ugh!, one unpleasant job after the next.
So you're a gunsmith?
Gunsmith... I am yet to earn that title. I've been tinkering with these wonderful devices for the past few years.
Turning scraps into deadly firearms – or augmenting la puissance and précision of a War-era instrument – such is my art, my métier, which I've found much too recently...
So I have much to learn. Under someone like Grigory – yes, I would be happy to seek his apprenticeship... But with this much work, there is no time.
Grigory, the trader up near the Hospital?
Yes, the same. That man has an aura of... Confidence. Fermeté in all of his responses and attitudes. That is worth gold, Returner.
He only sells guns, I think...
No, no, mon ami. He tinkers with them too, and quite expertly at that. You must not have paid much attention. Look beyond your preconceptions!
Can't really vouch for the quality of his wares...
Why, but they have a beauty and are well-designed... Not that I've used many guns myself, but I have it on good word that a weapon from Grigory is une bonne affaire.
Why do you talk... Weird, like that?
Like what? Ah, comme ça? Ha ha! There is nothing weird about it. It turns out, Returner, we were imbibed in the West's culture long before they dropped their bombs on us.

These little bits and pieces I remember of one of the West's many languages... They come from the conversations of nobility, of the old, pre-War rulers of our Continent... My parents were very cultured, and they taught me a bit.
Why bother talking in that tongue still?
In a just world, we would still be in contact with the West – a world my mother and father got to see for a bit, but which is lost to us now.
I, for one, simply enjoy the sounds and stories I associate with this Western language. They flow out of me naturally.
So... Everyone here used to know that weird language?
Well, not everyone. It was a lingua franca: a diplomatic and cultural necessity for our leaders and nobles.
Not just diplomacy, but also the greatest arts and sciences of all time were produced with it: learned men had to learn it to obtain any success in life. Such was the case with my father.
Never mind; I have to go.
Yes, yes, I've a simple task for you. Things are busy, I can't keep up with all the requests from these useless Rada – so I asked Sontse for an assistant, and he never showed! It's been days!
He must've died on the way over. Our Palatine friends could not find a body, however, so, hypothesis: his corpse has already been taken to Dazbog Hollow by the Mudlarks. Rotten fucking luck!

But I must prove to Sontse that the boy has died, or they will not send me a new one, the bureaucrats. Finding the signed Work Order he surely carried would be the proof I need. So won't you venture to Dazbog and find it for me?
Search corpses at Dazbog for a "work order". I can do that.
Good. But just in case – search your mind for questions now.
Got some questions first.
Well, sure, fair enough. What is it?
Sounds sketchy – not interested.
Why? Isn't this what you do for a living? C'est absurde.
How do you know the assistant's dead?
All good scientists work off an initial hunch, see, which they then try to disprove to avoid confirmation bias.

The young and weak often die in Zalesye, simple as their tasks may be. I hired Palatines to search for him along the route to Sontse and they came up short. Come on, Returner. What else could have happened?
Well, I suppose he could still be alive, but if that's the case – please find him, kill him and take the papers anyway. If he is this slow, he is no good for me.
You have means. Why not get someone else to help?
Usually I would use my status to get some Palatines to look into this to the end. But they are bad with the corpse-bearers, and my status is shot since I've been doing such menial work for the Rada.
I was considering bidding farewell to the promise of an assistant, Returner, but then you came along! You have a certain je ne sais quois; I feel that I can trust you with this.
I don't have any more questions.
Very well, then. In that case... Hop to it! Au travail!
My decision...
Yes?
Have you found my dead boy and his work order, Returner?
Not yet.
Need I remind you that the boy's corpse could be thrown in the Lake any time, now? Meaning, no reward for you. Hurry up!
Had some questions, actually.
Agh, vraiment? Okay, ask away.
Hmm, let's see. Looks like his papers are in order, if a bit scruffed. You did well. This should suffice for me to request a new assistant – and also for him to be properly escorted this time.
One measly Palatine to take that Mutant bite in the next boy's place – is that too much to ask, Returner?
Don't care. My reward?
Of course, pardon. Here it is, Returner.
No, it's not, Casmir. And my reward?
Right, right. Here you go – you've more than earned it! Tu l'as bien gagné!
